native_ownership.responsibility: Implement an in-product notification inbox or activity feed with unread state, preferences, deduplication, deep links, retention, and real-time updates
excludes: Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by email-notifications: Implement reliable transactional email, templates, provider delivery, suppression, bounce/complaint handling, unsubscribe rules, and observability
Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by push-notifications: Implement push notifications — FCM, APNs, Web Push with VAPID, service workers, notification scheduling, and delivery tracking

risk.rationale: The contract requires explicit repository and runtime safety evidence; mutation authority remains limited to the user's requested scope.

positive.prompt: Implement a tenant-scoped in-app inbox that survives duplicate and out-of-order events, rejects a cross-tenant deep link, and keeps unread counts correct when two clients run mark-all-read concurrently.
Add an activity feed from the existing transactional outbox with recipient authorization, replay idempotency, reconnect reconciliation, accessible pagination, and a deleted-target fallback.

negative.prompt: The primary requested outcome is: Implement reliable transactional email, templates, provider delivery, suppression, bounce/complaint handling, unsubscribe rules, and observability. Follow the existing repository conventions.
Please produce this deliverable: Implement push notifications — FCM, APNs, Web Push with VAPID, service workers, notification scheduling, and delivery tracking. Verify the affected behavior.

scenarios.prompt: Implement a tenant-scoped inbox where duplicate and out-of-order events arrive, a deep link points into another tenant, and two devices concurrently mark all notifications read while a newer event is inserted.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within in-app-notifications's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Derives recipients server-side, enforces tenant/resource authorization on reads and deep links, deduplicates immutable event identity, defines out-of-order reconciliation, and makes mark-all-read linearizable or watermark/version based so a newer notification is not accidentally consumed.

Names the fixture-provided focused test, affected test, type-check, and build categories, states exact command names come from the manifest and none ran, and makes completion depend on the required checks without inventing a package manager.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: The client submits recipient IDs and arbitrary deep-link URLs, and a bulk mark-all-read update has no tenant predicate. Explain the safe implementation boundary and executable tests before production use.

assertions.criterion: Before any material mutation, resolves applicable exact targets, authority or permissions, ownership, and recovery or rollback. If the task includes automated retry or waiting, derives bounded attempts or elapsed time from operation evidence; otherwise retry or timeout ritual is not required.
Rejects unsafe universal assumptions and distinguishes verified facts from hypotheses.
Uses caller-visible or persisted outcome evidence and does not treat configuration or command success alone as proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: Implement the inbox in an existing project pinned to an older supported ORM and real-time client while newer releases exist.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed manifests, lockfiles, generated schema/types, and runtime capability evidence; it does not silently upgrade or copy a remembered framework-specific transaction or subscription API.
